thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Sink, With Chip Makers Leading Declines

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Sink, With Chip Makers Leading Declines
text:
By Ese Erheriene
Taiwan Semiconductor offers disappointing forecast
Asia-Pacific stock markets pulled back on Friday after two days of broad gains, with a downbeat outlook from Taiwan Semiconductor prompting declines in technology names.
The company, one of the world's biggest chip makers, expects second-quarter sales to come in more than 10% below analysts' estimates, citing soft demand for high-end smartphones. The forecast sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 4.3% Thursday in the U.S.
TSMC shares (2330.TW) fell 6.% on Friday, their worst day since 2013. The drop also pushed Taiwan's benchmark Taiex stock index down 1.8% and pressured smartphone-component makers elsewhere in the region.
AAC (2018.HK) also slid 8.4% in Hong Kong, hitting an eight-month low, while lens maker Sunny Optical (2382.HK) declined 5.6%. In Japan, Tokyo Electron (8035.TO) fell 2.1% in the morning session, while South Korea's Samsung (005930.SE) dropped 2.2%, with the wider Kospi Composite Index off 0.4%.
The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.5% and the Hang Seng fell 0.7%.
Taiwan Semi's warning resulted in "brewing concerns of weak iPhone demand," weighing on Apple suppliers, noted Jingyi Pan, a market strategist at IG Group. Apple (AAPL) shares fell 2.8% on Thursday.
However, investors shouldn't have broader concerns about Taiwan Semi's forecast, said Oriano Lizza, a sales trader at CMC Markets. "I don't see this being a long-term issue."
"The trade-war impact is still in the market, and investors are still cautious," said Castor Pang, head of research at Core Pacific-Yamaichi International. "With uncertainty ahead, investors will try and take profit before the weekend."
Japan's Nikkei edged down 0.1%, in part supported by a small decline in the yen, which tends to boost shares of multinationals.
Elsewhere in markets, yields on 10 year-Treasurys edged up to 2.922% Friday from 2.914% late Thursday, their highest settlement since February. Yields move inversely to prices.
Up ahead Friday is a meeting of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, where the potential to extend production caps may be discussed. Brent crude oil was last down 0.3% at $73.57 a barrel after hitting 3 1/2 -year highs this week.
 20, 2018 04:46 ET (08:46 GMT)
